post.caption:
Deep Blue beat Kasparov in 1997; robots that walk reliably over uneven ground took another twenty years. Chess has a fixed board, full visibility and a turn to think. Balance has none of that. Standing still is already a controlled fall corrected hundreds of times a second by ankle, hip, inner ear and foot, and walking is falling forward and getting a leg out in time. You find it easy because you never had to know you were doing it.
